inline_comments.comment: Event name mismatch: the handler is registered with `server.watcher.on('all', watcherChangeHandler)` (line ~157) but deregistered here with `'change'`. Chokidar's `.off()` is a no-op when the event name doesn't match how the handler was registered, so the handler is never actually removed. After `bail()`, the 'all' listener will continue firing on the closed/recycled server. The fix is to use `'all'` here to match registration.

`waitForModuleGraph` is declared as a local `const` inside `start()`, so `bail()` has no reference to it and cannot call `clearInterval()`. If `bail()` is invoked while the module graph is still empty (i.e. before the interval self-clears on line 152), the interval will keep firing every second against an already-closed server. Store the handle at module scope (alongside `debounce` and `watcherChangeHandler`) and clear it inside `bail()`.

Subscribing to the `'all'` Chokidar event means `watcherChangeHandler` is also called for `addDir`, `unlinkDir`, and `error` events — directory-level changes that don't affect the module graph. Consider subscribing to the three specific events that actually matter (`'change'`, `'add'`, `'unlink'`) instead of using `'all'`, and update the `bail()` cleanup accordingly.

The `setInterval` callback is `async`, but `setInterval` ignores the returned Promise. If `server.waitForRequestsIdle()` rejects, the error is silently dropped — no log, no cleanup, no notification to callers of `onModuleGraphChange`. Wrap the body in a try/catch (or restructure so errors propagate) to handle this failure path.

`importers` and `importedModules` are typed as `Set<object>` to avoid importing Vite's types, but this causes a type safety hole: when the sets are iterated, each element is inferred as `object`, which does not satisfy the expected `{ file, type, importers, importedModules }` parameter shape of the recursive `getOrCreateModuleNode` call on lines 83 and 89. TypeScript strict mode should flag this. Consider defining a local recursive interface (e.g. `interface ViteModuleNodeLike { file: string | null; type: ModuleNode['type']; importers: Set<ViteModuleNodeLike>; importedModules: Set<ViteModuleNodeLike>; }`) and using it throughout.

The assertion checks that `watcher.off` was called with `'change'`, but the implementation registers the handler on `'all'` — so the correct event to verify deregistration for is `'all'`. The fake watcher's `off` implementation only removes from the matching event bucket, so with the current mismatch the 'all' listener is actually never removed during the test either. This test gives false confidence: it passes because `listeners.clear()` prevents `cb` from being notified, not because cleanup is correct. Fix the assertion to `toHaveBeenCalledWith('all', expect.any(Function))`.

The `onModuleGraphChange` callback only receives a `ModuleGraph` on success, with no way to signal failure states (timeout waiting for the graph to initialize, server errors, etc.). Callers have no way to distinguish a healthy graph update from a scenario where change detection is silently broken. Consider making the callback parameter a tagged-union event type, e.g. `{ type: 'moduleGraph'; moduleGraph: ModuleGraph } | { type: 'unavailable'; reason: string } | { type: 'error'; error: Error }`, so consumers can react appropriately to startup failures.

general_comments.comment: Module-level mutable singletons (`listeners`, `debounce`, `watcherChangeHandler`) mean calling `start()` a second time without an intervening `bail()` will create a new `watcherChangeHandler` closure, overwrite the module-level reference, and leave the previous handler still subscribed to `'all'` with no way to remove it. A subsequent `bail()` will only remove the most recent handler. Either enforce a single active lifecycle (guard against double-start) or encapsulate all per-server state in a class/factory so each instance owns its own state.

`buildModuleGraph` is a pure conversion utility with no side effects, but it lives in `index.ts` alongside lifecycle functions (`start`, `bail`, `onModuleGraphChange`). Moving it to a dedicated `utils/build-module-graph.ts` file would improve discoverability, make it easier to unit-test in isolation without mocking `createViteServer`, and keep `index.ts` focused on the builder lifecycle contract.
